signals.headline: Marlowe Foods raised a growth round
signals.fact: Marlowe Foods announced a growth round from a regional food fund on October 20.
signals.means: New money usually comes with a plan the investor has already seen: more volume, a wider customer list, or both. The team then has a few months to show that the plant and the paperwork can carry it.
signals.idea: List the three promises in the funding plan that depend on the plant, and give each one an owner and a date. Review the list monthly.
signals.source_label: Marlowe Foods raises a growth round from a regional food fund

signals.headline: A second packaging line is coming to the Ohio plant
signals.fact: Marlowe Foods announced a second packaging line at its Ohio plant on October 8.
signals.means: A second line often exposes what one line hid: changeover time, label checks and the hours a shift lead spends on handoffs. Output tends to rise before the routines around it catch up.
signals.idea: Time one changeover on the first line this week and write the steps as a checklist. Use it to set up the second line.
signals.source_label: Marlowe Foods adds a second packaging line at its Ohio plant

signals.headline: Marlowe Foods is hiring a head of quality
signals.fact: A head of quality role is open on the Marlowe Foods careers page, seen on September 29.
signals.means: A first head of quality is often hired when retail buyers start asking for audit records, or when the volume is too high for the founders to check by eye.
signals.idea: Collect every audit request and customer complaint from the past year in one sheet before the hire starts. It becomes their first week of work.
signals.source_label: Marlowe Foods is hiring a head of quality

data.note: I put these three together because each one asks more of the plant than it did a quarter ago: more money, more capacity and a new person to hold quality. Nothing here needs an answer. If it is useful, reply and tell me which part. If it is not, tell me and I will stop writing.
